messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for service=model-runtime (model-runner) in prod-west. Error spike started ~2199998860. Escalation level: P1. Paging on-call.
samir: oncall here, seeing it. Confirming impact: which customers hit? any downstream gateways reporting timeouts?
morgan: I'm tailing logs now, looks like repeated segfaults in model_runner process, lots of OOM-killer entries on node gpu-17.
anya: @samir can you check runbook 'runtime-crash-oom' and start handoff if needed? I'll notify CS.
samir: on it. Runbook step 1: collect pod restarts and coredumps. Running kubectl now.

samir: ```
kubectl get pods -n prod | grep model-runner | grep CrashLoop
model-runner-5b7c9   2/3     CrashLoopBackOff   5          21m
model-runner-9d4a1   3/3     Running           0          6m
``` 
morgan: grabbing node logs:

morgan: ```
[OOM] PID 23814(model_runner) killed by OOM-killer, total_rss: 62.1G, threshold: 60.0G
[segfault] signal 11 at 0x7f8c1b2e
stack: runtime::AttentionKernel::invoke+0x1a
``` 

leo: node gpu-17 memory pressure high, eviction of cache daemon happened. There's also a recent kernel module gpu-quantization. Any deploys in last hour?
anya: No prod deploys from redwood-deploy in last 2 hours. CI shows a canary to model-v2-quant at 2199998800 but not full roll.
samir: hypothesis: quantized kernel causing memory blowup under certain sequence lengths. Mitigation options: 1) route traffic to model-v2-fallback (non-quantized), 2) scale dedicated pool, 3) restart affected nodes after cordon.

jess: CS: two enterprise customers reporting errors (AcmeCorp, PaperTrail). Estimated error rate ~14% overall, spikes to 40% for longer inputs.
ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2214, linked in #incidents and PagerDuty.

samir: I'll start traffic reroute to fallback model and add circuit-breaker rules to reduce long-sequence requests hitting quant kernels.
morgan: while rerouting, capturing a core dump for analysis. Please avoid full node reboot until we snapshot.

samir: ```
# temporarily change routing
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model_priority":["model-v2-fallback","model-v2-quant"]}'
``` 

samir: routing change applied. Monitoring error rate.
morgan: error rate down to 2.6% in the next 30s. Crash count on gpu-17 decreased.
anya: good. I notified AcmeCorp SOC and CS with ETA for full mitigation: 15-30m. jess confirming.
jess: sent note to contacts, offered rollback guidance if they see bad outputs. They're happy with reroute for now.

leo: pro tip: I'm marking gpu-17 unschedulable (cordon) to avoid new heavy jobs and will drain non-critical pods.
leo: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-17
kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
``` 

morgan: core dump uploaded to s3://redwood-cores/2199998888/model_runner_gpu17_core.tar.gz, link added to INC-2214.
samir: I'm opening a postmortem stub and assigning follow-ups: root cause analysis, kernel module bisect, better mem-limits on quant runner, graceful degradation when KV cache growth > threshold.

anya: ops ask: do we need to rollback quant kernel canary from canary pool? leo: recommended: rollback canary to remove quant kernel until we reproduce locally.

samir: action items captured:
- [ ] keep route to fallback until next canary proven safe (samir)
- [ ] reproduce OOM locally with sequence-length test vectors (morgan)
- [ ] disable quant kernel in canary and redeploy (leo)
- [ ] notify customers with RCA and interim mitigation (jess/anya)

morgan: quick debug note — KV cache growth correlated with request prefix length > 1024 tokens for a particular workflow. Suggest adding defensive limit for KV cache per-session.
samir: adding cache limit to runtime config as temporary guard.

samir: ```
# patch config
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"kv_cache_per_session_mb":"512"}}'
``` 

samir: patched, rolling reload triggered. Monitoring.
morgan: after both reroute + cache guard, error rate back to baseline ~0.4%. No new crashes for 15m.
anya: handing off to follow-up rotation. @morgan @leo pls continue investigation during daytime. I'll keep CS looped.

jess: Customer update: AcmeCorp acknowledged mitigation, PaperTrail saw reduced errors and closed their emergency call. We scheduled follow-up call tomorrow.

samir: thanks all. Incident P1 -> moving to post-incident review. Leaving thread open for any late alerts.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2214 updated: status=mitigated, severity=P1, lead=samir, handoff_to=follow-up-team. Logs and core dump attached.
